subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a name possibly derived from Daz'issin, a diminutive form used by mothers in Menzoberranzan for sons they hoped would survive; his identity is entangled with erased records and a missing appendix in a heraldic text.
source_quote: I asked her directly who this Daz'issin was. She told me it was a softening name. That mothers use it for boys they wanted to live.

subject: Yvenne
fact: Yvenne is the archivist who holds the public record of Menzoberranzan; she speaks only within the limits of sealed records, but her body language betrays concealed knowledge — her stillness contradicts her words, signaling she knows more than she is permitted to say.
source_quote: I looked at her. At the way she was sitting. At the way she had been sitting for the last several minutes — the practiced stillness of someone who knows more than the public record allows her to say.

subject: Houses of Menzoberranzan
fact: Several houses in Menzoberranzan used the name Daz'issin, but most of them were eradicated; the act of striking a record — particularly the fourth seat with ritual archive privileges — was not mere political erasure but a costly, infrastructure-dependent act of total deletion requiring payment and plausible deniability.
source_quote: The fourth seat holds ritual archive privileges... a struck fourth seat was not merely a political erasure. It was the expensive kind. The kind that requires knowing the right people and paying the right price.

subject: erasure of Daz'issin records
fact: A deliberate, mechanical removal of an appendix from the book *Geography and Cities, Menzoberranzan, Pillars of Woe* occurred at least fifty years ago — likely to conceal the true identity and lineage of Daz'issin, suggesting a targeted suppression of personal and familial history.
source_quote: I looked at the cut. It was mechanical. A razor. Not age, not water damage... someone had taken to this book and removed what the footnote pointed to.

subject: *Geography and Cities, Menzoberranzan, Pillars of Woe*
fact: A two-hundred-year-old heraldic text with a missing appendix; the footnote referencing the appendix pointed to the name Daz'issin, and its removal was done with precision — indicating an intentional act of historical concealment.
source_quote: The footnote referenced an appendix. The appendix was missing.

subject: Daz's true origin
fact: Daz may be the last living bearer of the name Daz'issin — a name tied to extinct houses and erased records — and his survival may be linked to a protected lineage that was deliberately hidden, making his identity a living anomaly in Menzoberranzan’s official history.
source_quote: I asked if she knew my name. She did. I asked whether someone might call me Daz, and this was actually a name that, like, my mother used.

subject: The Sealed Records of Menzoberranzan
fact: The library is reputed to contain all information in the world, yet critical records — particularly those tied to Daz'issin and the fourth seat — are absent, implying the archive itself has been weaponized to suppress truth.
source_quote: This is a library with, by reputation, all the information in the world. Something is not here that should be here.

subject: Mercenaries following Daz
fact: Daz is simultaneously guarded and hunted by mercenary factions — one group ensuring his survival, another attempting to kill him — suggesting his existence is both valuable and dangerous to powers within Menzoberranzan.
source_quote: We have mercenaries following me around, trying to make sure I live, and other mercenaries following me around, trying to kill me.

subject: fifty years ago
fact: The appendix containing the name Daz'issin was physically removed from the book at least fifty years ago — a timestamp aligning with the last known usage of the name and the extinction of its associated houses.
source_quote: A razor, at least fifty years ago, someone had taken to this book and removed what the footnote pointed to.

subject: Daz'issin
fact: Daz'issin — lit. 'small shadow' — is a historical name used sparingly in Menzoberranzan; those who bore it were typically children of mothers seeking to protect them from the city’s lethal politics, and nearly all such houses were later struck from the records.
source_quote: Daz'issin, and lit., 'small shadow'... mothers use it for boys they wanted to live.
